nodes.title: Blender path – set once (clean Blender recommended)
PixelArtistry · Settings (high-poly)
widgets_values:
### Settings by VRAM (WTiVo)

| VRAM | WTiVo input_res = final_res | proxy_points |
|---|---|---|
| 6 GB | 1024 | lower it if you run out of memory |
| 8 GB+ | 1536 | 12,000,000 (default here) |
| 16 GB+ | 2048 – use the 2K preset (01b) | 25,000,000 with Quad Reconstruct bypassed (see 01b) |

**Proxy points:** more points let WTiVo follow more of the raw surface – more detail, but also more faces, RAM and time. 12M is the value that keeps the whole chain watertight in our tests; if you raise it, check the result with Blender's 3D Print Toolbox.

**Quad Reconstruct:** keep `resolution` at 1536. It flattens tiny surface detail – bypass it (Ctrl+B) if you need that detail.

**WTiVo `lambda_fill`:** 20 works for most models. 10–20 for small holes, 30–40 for big ones. Too high closes openings you want to keep (hoods, sleeves).

**LODTailor (step 4):** rebuilds WTiVo's 20–50M-face mesh with a fine voxel remesh in Blender (`relative_voxel_size` 0.001) and caps it at 6M faces – lighter, and still closed.

**WTiVo `component_mode` = largest:** keeps only the main piece and drops loose fragments. Switch to `auto` if your model has separate parts you want to keep.

**Holes in the result?** Run again – the structure seed is set to *randomize*, every run is a new generation.

nodes.title: B · Bake Forger (normal, AO, emission → kept in final)
PixelArtistry · Settings (low-poly)
widgets_values:
### Settings in this workflow (05p, prop)

**LODTailor (A):** `target_tris` **2,000** (props: 500–2,000). `relative_voxel_size` 0.0015 keeps thin parts such as a blade.

**Bake Forger (B):** all maps at **2048**; `tight_cage_extrusion_factor` **0.019** (hard-surface).

**UltraTex:** same as workflow 05 (4 steps, 12/6 views, `keep_existing` UVs).

---

*General notes from workflow 02:*

### Low-poly + baking

**LODTailor (A):** `target_tris` 20–30k for characters, 500–1,000 for props. `relative_voxel_size` 0.0015 for organic shapes, 0.05 for hard-surface (keeps sharper edges). More `passes` = better result, but slower.

**Bake Forger (B):** all maps at 4096 – set the `*_resolution` values to 2048 or 8192 if you like. `tight_cage_extrusion_factor`: 0.0019 for characters, 0.019 for hard-surface – raise it if white patches appear on the low-poly.

**Fast Merge (C):** welds duplicate vertices and tiny gaps of the baked low-poly in `TEXTURE_SAFE` mode, so the UVs stay intact. If it can't close the mesh, it passes the file through unchanged. No Blender needed.

**Checking in Blender:** import the textured low-poly with **Merge Vertices** ticked. A GLB can't give one vertex two UV coordinates, so UV seams otherwise show up as open edges.

**Blender:** LODTailor and Bake Forger read the path from the *Blender path* node. Use a clean Blender without add-ons (portable install) – add-ons like Auto-Rig Pro can break headless runs.

**Output:** `output/3d/PixelArtistry_lowpoly_*.glb` – the baked game-ready asset.

nodes.title: PixelArtistry · Start here
widgets_values:
# PixelArtistry · 05p Image → Game-ready Prop (low-poly + UltraTex)

The prop version of workflow 05, used for the sword in the video: same chain, tuned for hard-surface props. Output `output/3d/PixelArtistry_sword_final_*.glb`.

To give a character a weapon for ActionForge: put the prop into the character's hand in Blender, keep it a **separate object**, export both as one GLB, and tag the prop piece as **prop** in ActionForge's rigger.

## Before the first run
1. Run the installer from https://github.com/pixelartistry/PixelArtistry-Animated-Characters (it fills in the Blender path).
2. **UltraTex scratch folder** node: set `spill_directory` to a drive with free space.
3. Load your prop image: the whole object, straight front view, plain background.

---

# PixelArtistry · Image → Game-Ready 3D Asset

Free & local ComfyUI workflow by **PixelArtistry**.

## How to use
1. Load your image in **Load Image** (green group).
2. Set your Blender path once in **Blender path** (purple group 1).
3. Choose the model with **Boolean (Switch to Trellis2)**: `false` = Pixal3D, `true` = Trellis.2
4. Set **LODTailor (A)** `target_tris`: 20–30k for characters, 500–1,000 for props.
5. Press **Run**.

## What happens
Pixal3D / Trellis.2 generate shape + texture → **Quad Reconstruct → WTiVo → LODTailor** make a watertight high-poly → it gets its textures (`PixelArtistry_highpoly`) → **LODTailor** builds the low-poly → **Bake Forger** bakes all maps onto it → **Fast Merge** welds duplicate vertices without breaking the UVs (`PixelArtistry_lowpoly`).

Both files land in `ComfyUI/output/3d/`.

## PixelArtistry
- Website: https://pixel-artistry.com
- YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@PixelArtistry_
- X: https://x.com/philippsieben
- Newsletter FutureFrames: https://go.pixel-artistry.com/newsletter

## Built with MostAadTech's nodes
The watertight, low-poly and baking steps in this workflow run on free, open-source ComfyUI nodes by **MostAadTech**. He spent over a month building them and was a huge help while these workflows were made – please show him some love:

- **Quad Reconstruct** – cleans the raw mesh and removes floating fragments
- **Memory Cleaner** – frees VRAM between the heavy steps
- **WTiVo** – makes the mesh watertight
- **LODTailor** – builds the lighter or low-poly mesh in Blender
- **Bake Forger** – bakes the high-poly maps onto the low-poly
- **Fast Merge** – welds duplicate vertices for a clean final file

**Follow & support MostAadTech**

- Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/cw/MostafaAwad/membership
- GitHub: https://github.com/Mstafa-awad

Qwen GGUF: `unsloth/Qwen3-8B-GGUF`. **Q4_K_M** because the text encoder only encodes an **empty prompt**, so a smaller quant costs practically nothing and saves VRAM. Have `Qwen3-8B-Q6_K.gguf`? Just pick it here.

nodes.title: Read me · Models

widgets_values:
## 3 · Prepare
Renders the normal views and lines your reference up with the front camera.

**Check the three previews before a long run:**
- **Normal views:** your mesh from all sides.
- **Aligned reference:** the object should fill the silhouette **edge to edge**.
- **Aligned mask:** white object on black.

Small or shifted? Check `mask_polarity`: **foreground** for BiRefNet, **background** if you use Load Image's own MASK instead.
nodes.title: Read me · Prepare

widgets_values:
## 4 · Generate views
**All quality and speed settings live on the two Generate nodes.**

| Setting | Albedo | MR | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view_resolution` | **1024** | 1024 | 6 GB: 1024 · 8 GB: up to 1536–2048 |
| `view_count` | **12** | **6** | 12 = 6 + a guided 45° pass |
| `steps` | **4** | 4 | dev: 4 is enough, 8 is better |
| `extra_angle_mode` | guided | – | 45° pass starts from pass 1 |

- **Same seed** on both Generate nodes.
- **Steps are the speed lever.** Time scales with steps. Compare 4 / 8 / 25 on your asset and judge the back and sides, not just the front.
- MR maps are low-detail, so **6 views** are enough there.
- `tiled_decode` **on** for low VRAM.
nodes.title: Read me · Generate

widgets_values:
## 5 · Bake & save
Bakes albedo and MR views onto the **one shared UV layout**. Saves to `output/ultratex/`:
- textured **GLB** (+ Preview 3D)
- **base color**, **roughness** and **metallic** maps as separate PNGs

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `texture_size` | 2048 (4096 for hero assets, same VRAM, slower bake) |
| `fill_unseen` | on: estimates hidden areas (no new detail) |
| `blend_mode` | detail_preserving |
| `repair_mode` | normal_aware_surface |

Faceted face? Try `normal_mode = preserve` vs `smooth` in Prepare.
